name: Go Fashion (India) Ltd
title: Go Fashion (India) Ltd - 543401 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Go Colors Q1 FY27 shows first positive EBO SSSG (0.6%) and 66 store closures, but EBITDA fell 2% to INR67.4cr, inventory is INR245cr at ~100 days, and fabric costs are up 7–10% with no price hikes taken.

summary.headline: Go Fashion Q1 FY27: EBITDA before exceptionals down 2% to INR67.4 crores on marketing spend, while EBO SSSG turned positive at 0.6%.
summary.overview: Revenue was flat YoY at about INR223 crores with gross margin of 62.9%, and EBITDA before exceptional items was INR67.4 crores (30.3% margin), down 2%. Management attributed the EBITDA moderation mainly to higher marketing spend, including the brand ambassador partnership. A one-off exceptional charge of INR6.5 crores was booked for write-off of capex on 66 closed stores, and PAT was about INR16 crores. Management presented the quarter as early progress against five FY27 priorities but repeatedly cautioned that one quarter does not make a trend.

segments.name: EBO (company-operated stores)
segments.commentary: SSSG +0.6% and same cluster sales growth +1.2%; footfall up about 1-1.5% YoY per bill cuts. Stores above 700 sq ft delivered SSSG of roughly 2.5%-3%, over 130 such stores.

segments.name: LFS (large format stores, Reliance Trends channel)
segments.commentary: Grew 2% YoY to INR50 crores after a difficult FY26; management says supply-chain disruption with a key LFS partner in Q3-Q4 FY26 has largely normalised.

segments.name: Everyday wear (daily wear concept)
segments.commentary: 15 stores live; 12-13 stated as profitable, with about 12 double-digit EBITDA positive. Sales around INR1,000 per sq ft per month. Target of 25-30 stores by end FY27. Size requirement 1,500-2,000 sq ft.

guidance_outlook: Store footprint: square feet to rise about 8%-10% on a year-through basis in FY27, back-ended; closures expected to be much lower than in recent quarters, though no store-count guidance given.
Advertising spend to stay within 2%-3% of revenue in FY27.
Everyday wear stores targeted at 25-30 by end FY27, from 15 today; 10-12 new product refreshes planned for FY27.
Company-level inventory days expected at 90-100 by year-end, including daily wear; working capital days have room to improve by a few days.
Capex to be funded through internal accruals; new large stores assumed 15-20 month payback and 45-60 days inventory on sales.
Fabric costs up 7%-10%; management is not taking price hikes now and expects gross margin pressure in coming quarters, magnitude not quantified.
capex_capacity: Store network: 66 stores closed in Q1, reducing retail space by 7,000 sq ft; further larger-format stores to be added in catchments where small stores are closed.
Plan to expand footprint over five years with potential to double square feet deployed, across Tier 1, 2 and 3 cities.
New store unit economics: payback 15-20 months, inventory turns 45-60 days on sales for larger stores.
Exceptional INR6.5 crores capex write-off linked to store closures in Q1.
Lingerie and ladies innerwear under evaluation as an addition to the daily wear concept.
demand_pricing: EBO SSSG +0.6% in Q1; management attributes it to possibly a weak base, transfer of sales from closed stores, and better Q1 footfalls, and says it is too early to call a trend.
Full price sales 94%; ASP about INR863.
Fabric cost inflation of 7%-10% linked to Middle East disruption; no price hikes taken yet.
Brand ambassador Shraddha Kapoor onboarded from July 2026 to target a younger audience.
Management said malls and high streets show no real outlier in SSSG, and older 700+ sq ft stores show a similar trend.

qa_highlights.question: What net retail area growth is expected in FY27, and is it back-ended?
qa_highlights.answer: Square feet deployed to rise about 8%-10% on a 12-month basis; the quarter alone saw a 7,000 sq ft reduction, and the increase will come over the year.

qa_highlights.question: What would SSSG look like excluding closed or to-be-closed stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Reported SSSG excludes stores closed in Q1 but not future closures. 700+ sq ft stores grew about 2.5%-3%; management could not give a clean ex-closures figure and attributed the 0.6% to base effects, transfers and footfall.

qa_highlights.question: How many more store closures in FY27 and how far through is the process?
qa_highlights.answer: No numeric guidance; closures depend on large-store opportunities but are expected to be much lower than in recent quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How much have raw material costs risen?
qa_highlights.answer: Fabric costs up 7%-10%; no price hike currently, and gross margin impact is hard to quantify given older inventory, though it is expected to hit coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What are SSSG trends by store vintage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no clean vintage correlation; some FY18 stores grew about 10% while some FY24 stores declined. Detailed bucket data to be sent later through SGA.

qa_highlights.question: How are everyday wear stores performing?
qa_highlights.answer: 15 stores live; about 12-13 profitable and 12 double-digit EBITDA positive; INR1,000 per sq ft monthly sales; actual size requirement 1,500-2,000 sq ft.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from fabric inflation of 7%-10%, with no price hikes yet and timing of pass-through uncertain.
SSSG sustainability: management explicitly said 0.6% is not a trend and the drivers are not clearly separated.
LFS dependence on Reliance Trends; speculation about partner format conversion to AZORTE, which management could not assess.
Marketing spend elevated (2.3% of revenue, with brand ambassador) with EBITDA already down 2%.
Management said it would clarify the earlier 10%-12% SSSG statement on ~275 stores via SGA; this is unresolved and a credibility question.
Inventory of INR245 crores and 139 working capital days; target to reduce inventory days to 90-100.

financial_highlights.change: revenue and gross margin stable vs Q1 last year
one-off write-off of capex on store closures
